seeds.text: Find the least positive integer n such that 10^n ≡ -1 (mod 23). If no such n exists, answer NONE.
seeds.human_solution: Since gcd(10, 23) = 1, the base is a unit modulo 23. The multiplicative order of 10 modulo 23 is d = 22. If 10^n ≡ -1 (mod 23) then squaring gives 10^(2n) ≡ 1, so d | 2n, while d does not divide n. Therefore n must be an odd multiple of d/2 = 11. Direct computation gives 10^11 ≡ 22 ≡ -1 (mod 23), so the exponent d/2 does produce -1. The least such n is therefore 11.
